title: A randomized clinical trial to investigate the influence of the healing procedure - closed vs. open healing - on the success rate of dental implants
summary:
In the event of tooth loss, a dental prosthesis can be attached using an implant inserted into the bone to restore function. The aim of this study is to clarify whether the surgical procedure has an influence on the success of the treatment. This may help us to further optimize the therapy in the future. 
The implant is inserted into the bone and replaces the tooth root. During the healing period, the implant should be able to heal for around 8 - 12 weeks without weight-bearing.  There are two different procedures: 
Firstly, the implant heals under the covering oral mucosa. This requires a second minor surgical procedure in which the implant is exposed and a so-called gingiva former, a healing cap for the mucous membrane, is inserted. The gingiva former is used to shape the mucous membrane at the transition of the implant between the bone and the oral cavity.
In the second procedure, the implant does not heal under the oral mucosa, but the implant is fitted with the gingiva former at the same time as the implant is placed. In the second procedure, no additional surgical intervention is necessary.
With this study, we want to investigate whether the healing procedure has an influence on the survival of the implant and the success of the therapy. We will collect clinical measurements such as pocket depths, the gap between the gum and the implant, around the implant or inflammation of the mucosa. X-rays are also taken as part of the usual implant aftercare. These images allow us to assess the strength of the implant in the bone. We will also ask you about your satisfaction with the implant prosthetic restoration and evaluate the benefits in relation to the costs and effort involved.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Interdental gaps in the maxillary and/or mandibular posterior region
- Free-end situations in the maxillary and/or mandibular posterior region
o The extraction was at least 3 months ago. Only early implantations (3 - 6 months post extraction) and late implantations (> 6 months post extraction) are performed. 
- A contralateral natural tooth must be present as a reference tooth, as well as antagonistic dentition.
- The patient has good oral hygiene and compliance.
- A pre-implant hygiene phase must have been completed.
- The patient's declaration of consent is available.
Exclusion criteria:
- Persons under 18 or persons lacking legal capacity
- Untreated acute periodontitis with pocket depths > 4 mm.
- Heavy smokers (more than 10 cigarettes per day)
- Taking bisphosphonates
- Pregnant women
- Alcohol or drug addicts
- Patients with an infectious disease such as hepatitis, HIV or AIDS
- Patients with severe diabetes mellitus.
- Immediate implantations
- Primarily recognizable need for augmentation
- Width of the gap in the mesio-distal direction for single-tooth gaps > 6.8 mm
